messages:
mike: quick q — proposal to compress routing/error tags in client-visible errors so the console shows one clear badge (degraded/healthy/rate_limited) instead of long route ids. lightweight RFC here: https://go/internal/rfc/compact-errors. thoughts?

sara: i'm worried about losing signal for triage. ops uses route_id in the payload to map to infra fast. if we hide it, we slow down incidents.

alex: can we split concerns: short badge for UI, but keep full routing detail in an internal header (x-rw-routing-detail) that only internal systems and support see? that keeps UX clean. :thumbsup:

jordan: +1 to alex. also need to unify 429 subcodes mapping — some SDKs treat any 429 as retryable. compacting shouldn't change retry semantics.

mike: example compacted payload i'm proposing:
```json
{"error":"rate_limited","client_code":"rate.limit","badge":"degraded"}
```
current payloads include route_id + route_path + tier + fallback_reason which is noisy in console.

rachel: small governance question — are we okay exposing labels like 'degraded' to customers? legal asked about wording that could be misinterpreted as SLA admission. maybe 'throttled' is safer.

ops-bot: incident-bot created INC-2026: track telemetry retention and route->badge backlinks for any regressions.

sara: if we remove route_id from the UI payload, the console must provide a backend hover/link that resolves badge->route(s). otherwise support can't jump straight to infra playbooks.

jordan: telemetry owners: please ensure logs still ingest route_id and tier as tags. proposed telemetry tag set: [route_id, route_tier, fallback_reason, subcode]. mark route_id as internal-only in public APIs.

devex-bot: reminder: SDKs currently strip unknown headers by default in some languages. devex will add guidance to preserve x-rw-* headers and expose retry-hint to users.

alex: rollout sketch: expose an opt-in header x-rw-compact-errors=true. run for 2 weeks behind the header, gather support ticket volume + search signal, then flip to default if clean.

mike: can someone own the canary and metric checklist?

chris: i can own canary. plan: 10% traffic for 72h. smoke metrics: console error-rate, untriaged incidents, support search match rate, and any increase in false-positive client-side handling. i'll post a runbook.

rachel: also add quality check against our eval prompt set to ensure compact badge doesn't break any client-side heuristics that parse error text.

sara: +1. ensure logs still include full context (request_id, route_id, model_variant) for oncall to triage.

mike: next steps: chris runs canary, devex updates SDK guidance + examples, i will open RFC PR with exact JSON shapes and header names and a copy of console mockups. thanks all :tada:

alex: small nit — pick stable header names now. propose: x-rw-compact-errors, x-rw-routing-detail, x-rw-retry-hint.

jordan: agree. also add a telemetry tag 'compact_error_version' so we can roll back easily in metrics.

mike: good call. I'll include that in the RFC. hitting backlog item after lunch.

chris: filed a small checklist in the canary ticket: smoke dashboards, alert thresholds, rollback steps. will ping when ready to start.

mike: awesome. tagging @sara @rachel @devex-bot for visibility. thanks everyone.
